content.text:
Your guess is right — and your reasoning is exactly the right reasoning.

**Why round wins:** with 4 tiles in the bag, 3 of them are round, so a random draw lands on round with probability 3/4 = 75%, and on square with probability 1/4 = 25%. Round is three times as likely.

**The part that often trips people up:** the *order* you put the tiles in doesn't matter. "I dropped the square in first, so it's at the bottom" and "the round ones are on top" would only matter if you grabbed from the top without mixing. A random draw treats every tile as equally likely regardless of position or insertion order. If instead you pulled a tile off the top of the bag, then order *would* matter — and round would be even more likely. So your answer was right under the harder assumption.

**The general rule to carry forward:** probability = (number of favorable outcomes) ÷ (number of equally likely outcomes). The size, shape, or color of the other tiles is irrelevant; only how many of them there are and how many are the one you want.

One more twist worth knowing: this only works because all four tiles are *equally likely* to be picked. If one tile were much bigger than the others, or if you were picking by feel through a cloth bag, the "equal likelihood" assumption would break and the simple count would no longer guarantee round is most likely.

Want me to run a quick simulation of random draws so you can see the ~3-in-4 pattern settle in empirically?
